instructions: Arrange the bresaola on a serving platter in an even layer, overlapping the slices slightly.
Squeeze 1 tablespoon of juice from the lemon into a bowl. Add the arugula, olive oil, salt and pepper and toss until coated.
Pile the dressed arugula on top of the bresaola.
Use a vegetable peeler to shave the Parmesan over the top and serve right away.
method_notes: America's Test Kitchen (the lead, 4.0 from 10, so a fallback lead) lays the bresaola on a plate, tosses the arugula in olive oil and lemon and piles it on with shaved Parmigiano. I doubled its two serving amounts for 4. The Italian Recipe Book dresses the bresaola itself with lemon, and Lidia Bastianich (Grana Padano) uses a whole lemon with zest. None of the others has ratings. I used the lead's method with a slightly bigger squeeze of lemon, to match the list's lemony line.
